title: auth 19: read the certificate's notAfter, so expiry is warned about (§5.4) and renewal is not by file age
design:
FOUND 2026-11-24, auditing what epic mimid-e13m shipped against
docs/design/frontend-auth.md. It is a gap in what steps 3, 8 and 9
delivered, recorded in three places as a limitation:

- crates/mimid-agent/src/tls.rs, module `# Limitations`: "No warning
  before expiry and no ERROR once expired (§5.4): the agent does not read
  the certificate's validity; clients' refusals are what show it."
- crates/mimid-agent/src/acme.rs, module `# Limitations`: "Renewal is by
  file age, not by the certificate's own notAfter nor by ARI."
- acme.rs `ASSUMED_LIFETIME`, 90 days, "since the agent does not read its
  own certificate back".

WHAT §5.4 ASKS FOR, exactly, and none of it is open:

- WARN from 14 days before expiry and ERROR from 3 days (INVENTED by the
  design note, so the numbers are settled).
- An expired certificate is still served, with an ERROR each hour, rather
  than closing the listener: clients will refuse it, and the log says why.
- Renewal starts at two thirds of the lifetime. That is already the rule;
  the bug is that "the lifetime" is assumed rather than read, so a
  certificate issued for an unusual lifetime renews on the wrong
  schedule. Let's Encrypt's six-day certificates would renew far too
  late.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A LOG LINE. `source = "files"` is the case that
matters most: the user's own certbot or `tailscale cert` timer can stop
working, and today the agent serves the stale certificate silently until
a client refuses it. The agent is the only thing watching that file.

WHAT TO BUILD.

A. Read `notAfter` (and `notBefore`) from the leaf DER. Nothing in the
tree parses X.509 today: rcgen writes, and rustls-webpki is a
dev-dependency that does not expose the field. So a minimal strict DER
walk, in its own module: Certificate SEQUENCE -> tbsCertificate SEQUENCE
-> skip the optional [0] version, the serialNumber INTEGER, the
signature AlgorithmIdentifier and the issuer Name -> the validity
SEQUENCE -> two Time values. RFC 5280 §4.1.2.5: UTCTime (tag 0x17,
YYMMDDHHMMSSZ, years 1950-2049) and GeneralizedTime (tag 0x18,
YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ), both ending in Z and nothing else, per §4.1.2.5.1 and
§4.1.2.5.2. Strict per AGENTS.md: definite lengths in their shortest
form, no trailing bytes, a named constant for every limit, and a failure
is "unknown", never a guess. `time` 0.3.55 is already a dependency and
turns the fields into a SystemTime with no new crate.

B. One place that decides, in tls.rs beside `Certificates`: given the
leaf's notAfter and now, which of nothing / WARN / ERROR / expired it is,
with EXPIRY_WARN_WITHIN = 14 days and EXPIRY_ERROR_WITHIN = 3 days as
named constants citing §5.4. The reload loop already runs on a timer and
is where the hourly ERROR belongs; it needs an EXPIRED_ERROR_EVERY of one
hour and the time of the last one, so a 60-second reload does not log 60
times an hour.

C. acme.rs's `past_renewal` takes the real lifetime when the leaf parses,
and keeps ASSUMED_LIFETIME only as the fallback for a certificate it
cannot read. local_ca.rs issues its own leaves and already knows
LEAF_VALID_DAYS, so it needs nothing, but it should use the same code
rather than keep its own rule.

TESTS, OFFLINE. rcgen is already there, so a test can issue a leaf with
any notAfter and assert the thresholds at a chosen `now`: inside 14 days
warns, inside 3 days errors, past notAfter is expired and still served,
and the hourly ERROR is not repeated inside the hour. Fixtures per
AGENTS.md come from outside the code under test: rcgen's DER for the
happy path, plus a hand-built UTCTime/GeneralizedTime pair with
byte-by-byte comments, and hostile input (a truncated validity, a
non-shortest length, trailing bytes, a Time without the Z, year 2050 in
a UTCTime).
